Let

\[
I=\int_{0}^{+\infty}\frac{x\log x}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}\,dx.
\]

### 1. Convergence

Near \(x=0\),

\[
\left|\frac{x\log x}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}\right|\le x|\log x|,
\]

and

\[
\int_{0}^{1}x|\log x|\,dx<\infty.
\]

Near \(x=\infty\),

\[
(x^{2}+1)^{2}\ge x^{4},
\]

so

\[
\left|\frac{x\log x}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}\right|
\le \frac{|\log x|}{x^{3}},
\]

and

\[
\int_{1}^{\infty}\frac{\log x}{x^{3}}\,dx<\infty.
\]

Thus the integral converges absolutely.

### 2. Evaluation

Since the integral is absolutely convergent, we may use the substitution \(x=1/t\). Then \(dx=-dt/t^{2}\), and

\[
\begin{aligned}
I
&=\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{x\log x}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}\,dx \\
&=\int_{\infty}^{0}
\frac{(1/t)\log(1/t)}{\left(1+1/t^{2}\right)^{2}}
\left(-\frac{dt}{t^{2}}\right) \\
&=\int_{\infty}^{0}\frac{t\log t}{(1+t^{2})^{2}}\,dt \\
&=-\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{t\log t}{(1+t^{2})^{2}}\,dt \\
&=-I.
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore \(I=-I\), so \(2I=0\), hence \(I=0\).

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
